The [hierarchical model](bayesian-inference.qmd#def-hierarchical-model) of [the two-level Gaussian example](bayesian-inference.qmd#exm-two-level-normal)
is the random-effects *model structure*,
with group-level parameters $\param_j \sim \ndist{\mean, \sdbetween^2}$
drawn from a common distribution.
What changes here from a maximum likelihood fit is the *inference method*:
the Bayesian analysis places priors on the hyperparameters $\mean$ and $\sdbetween$
and samples their joint posterior together with the group-level parameters
[@dobson4e, Chapter 14, p. 329].
The posterior shrinks each group's estimate toward the overall mean,
by an amount the data determine through $\sdbetween$,
and the posterior for $\sdbetween$ carries the uncertainty about the between-group spread
into every group-level summary.
